Seminar Title:

Plasma membrane lipid raft orchestrated signaling driven chromatin dynamics: deciphering the impact of hub genes and their epigenetic regulation by targeting EGFR-RAS-MAPK in colon adenocarcinoma

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

Life Science

Speaker Name:

Ankan Roy ( Rollno : 519ls1020)

Speaker Type:

Venue:

LS Seminar Room

Date and Time:

21 Aug 2026 12:00 noon

Contact:

Samir Kumar Patra

Abstract:

The role of plasma membrane lipid raft (PMLR) signaling in the epigenetic regulation of gene expression remains insufficiently characterized. The association between gene regulation and the dynamics of plasma membrane signaling hubs, particularly lipid rafts, is largely unexplored. Elucidating the oncogenic rewiring of mechanochemical signals from the plasma membrane to the chromatin territory, and clarifying the signaling axis that links PMLR dynamics to the epigenetic reprogramming of hub genes, is essential for understanding disease progression, including colon adenocarcinoma (COAD). Accordingly, this thesis is composed of the results obtained by investigation on how PMLR-mediated signaling pathways modulate epigenetic modifications of genes. COAD-specific hub genes (COL1A1, COL1A2, COL4A1, SPP1, SPARC, and THBS2) were identified through comprehensive bioinformatics analyses. The findings indicate that increased expression of these hub genes initiates and promotes COAD progression. The influence of PMLR dynamics on gene-specific promoter methylation was examined in COAD cells. Transient destabilization (TD) of lipid rafts, induced by ectopic cholesterol efflux, was found to activate the epidermal growth factor (EGF)-independent, lipid raft-associated EGFR-RAS-MAPK signaling pathway. This activation leads to increased expression of DNA methyltransferases (DNMTs) and decreased expression of hub genes in COAD cells. Subsequently, the effects of thymoquinone (TQ) and embelin (EB), both individually and in combination, were evaluated on cancer stem cell (CSC)-enriched colonospheres derived from HT29 and HCT15 cell lines. Analysis of EGFR-RAS-MAPK pathway components demonstrated that combinatorial treatment inhibits this pathway at multiple effectors and promotes the expression of specific collagen-synthesizing genes in colonospheres. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that TQ and EB can stably interact with key DNMTs and histone deacetylases (HDACs), potentially influencing their enzymatic activity. Therefore, the combined use of TQ and EB is proposed as a promising therapeutic epigenetic strategy. Inhibition of DNMT1, DNMT3A, DNMT3B, HDAC1, and HDAC2 by these phytochemicals may prevent colon cancer with reduced toxicity compared to synthetic drugs. RAS proteins harbouring specific mutations transmit oncogenic signals independently of EGFR activation. Consequently, novel compounds have been developed to target previously undruggable KRAS mutants using computer-aided drug design. Finally, the significance of signaling condensates at the plasma membrane, including PMLR-associated KRAS-GRB2-SOS1, and chromatin condensates, such as ZNF304-DNMT1-EZH2-SUV39H1/SUV39H2 at specific chromatin loci of CDKN2A and CDKN2B gene expression, was assessed.
